rules.title: Nondiscrimination in access to rental housing
rules.requirement: Covered housing providers must not discriminate on protected grounds when allowing applicants to view or rent an apartment, subject to the exemption for owner-occupied two-family dwellings.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to landlords, sellers and rental agents involved in residential apartment viewing or rental transactions in Cambridge, except two-family dwellings where the owner lives. Protected grounds identified by the source are disability, race, color, national origin or ancestry, family status, source of income including Section 8 and public benefits, marital status including married and non-married individuals, sex including allegations of sexual harassment, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, religious creed, military status, relationship status and family structure. The source defines disability consistently with the ADA as a physical or mental impairment substantially limiting one or more major life activities. The supplied vocabulary cannot fully represent the covered actors and transactions.
rules.exemptions: Two-family dwellings where the owner lives.
rules.quoted_span:
The Fair Housing Ordinance prohibits discrimination in real estate transactions such as:
viewing or renting an apartment
terms and conditions of tenancy
refusing to reasonably accommodate a person with a  disability if the accommodation would not cause an undue hardship to the landlord
viewing or purchasing a home
applying for or obtaining a mortgage
purchasing homeowners' or renters' insurance
printing, publicizing or advertising housing in a discriminatory manner
Under the law, landlords, sellers and rental agents may use any reasonable standard to determine which applicants are selected, as long as that standard is applied equally and uniformly to all applicants. Tenant selection may be based on:
an applicant's ability to pay the rent
an applicant's ability to take care of the apartment and to respect the rights of others
NOTE: there is an exemption for 2-family dwellings, when the owner lives there

rules.title: Reasonable and uniformly applied tenant-selection standards
rules.requirement: Landlords, sellers and rental agents must use reasonable applicant-selection standards and apply them equally and uniformly to all applicants, except at owner-occupied two-family dwellings. Permitted tenant-selection considerations include ability to pay rent, care for the apartment and respect others' rights.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to landlords, sellers and rental agents selecting applicants for residential rental housing in Cambridge. Two-family dwellings where the owner lives are exempt. The supplied fact vocabulary cannot establish whether the person conducting selection is a landlord, seller or rental agent; the fee-charger role fields do not establish those roles for tenant selection.
rules.exemptions: Two-family dwellings where the owner lives.

rules.title: Reasonable disability accommodation in rental access
rules.requirement: In covered residential rental transactions, landlords must not refuse a reasonable accommodation for a person with a disability when it would not cause the landlord undue hardship. Owner-occupied two-family dwellings are exempt.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to landlords in Cambridge residential rental transactions involving a person with a disability, including access to viewing or renting an apartment. Disability means a physical or mental impairment substantially limiting one or more major life activities, defined consistently with the ADA. The accommodation must be reasonable and must not cause undue hardship to the landlord; two-family dwellings where the owner lives are exempt. The supplied vocabulary cannot fully express landlord status, disability, accommodation reasonableness or undue hardship.
rules.exemptions: Two-family dwellings where the owner lives; the stated accommodation obligation is conditional on the accommodation not causing undue hardship to the landlord.

review.issue: The page describes current enforcement and operative prohibitions, supporting in_force status as of 2026-10-01, but supplies no effective date for the extracted duties. All effective_date values remain null; the Commission's establishment in 1984 is not an effective date for these provisions.
review.quoted_span:
The Cambridge Human Rights Commission (CHRC) was established in 1984 to protect the civil rights of residents and visitors to the city. The Commission enforces two ordinances: the
Cambridge Human Rights Ordinance, chapter 2.76
and the
Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance, chapter 14.04

review.issue: Remedies are stated in a separate passage and are therefore recorded here rather than added to requirements whose quotations do not contain them. Following probable cause, unsuccessful conciliation and a hearing, the Commission may file a criminal complaint in District Court, levy civil fines up to $300 for each violation, file a Superior Court civil complaint seeking injunctive relief, and seek damages, expenses and other relief. For a Fair Housing Ordinance complaint with probable cause, either party may elect removal to Superior Court for trial or to the Attorney General's Office for review and resolution.
review.quoted_span: If, during the Commission’s investigation, the evidence is sufficient to show that discrimination may have occurred (Probable Cause), the Commission will attempt conciliation between the parties. If the Commission’s conciliation efforts prove unsuccessful, it will schedule a public hearing at the Commission. The Commission has the authority to provide various remedies after hearing, including filing a criminal complaint in District Court, levying civil fines of up to $300 for each violation, filing a civil complaint in Superior Court seeking injunctive relief, and seeking an award of damages, expenses and other relief. If Probable Cause is found in a complaint filed under the Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance, either party may opt to remove the case for trial in the Massachusetts Superior Court or to the Attorney General’s Office for review and resolution.

review.issue: The protected-category definitions below inform the nondiscrimination and accommodation coverage. These conditions, covered actor roles and transaction scope require execution review because the supplied fact vocabulary cannot fully represent them.
review.quoted_span:
Discrimination occurs when a policy or practice segregates, creates unequal status, separates or has a disproportionate impact on a person based on their membership in one or more legally protected categories. The protected categories under the Cambridge Human Rights Ordinance and the Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance are the following:
Disability – Defined consistent with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) – a physical or mental impairment which substantially limits one or more major life activities
Race
Color
National Origin or Ancestry
Family Status
Source of Income, includes Section 8 and public benefits
Marital Status, includes married and non-married individuals
Sex: Male or female, includes allegations of sexual harassment
Gender identity or expression
Sexual Orientation: Heterosexual, homosexual, or bisexual
Age
Religious Creed
Military Status
Relationship Status
Family Structure
